business_problem: Merck needed to remove complexity and manual effort from the clinical trial process, where medical writers spent months reviewing thousands of pages of clinical data to produce regulatory-quality clinical study reports.
solution_summary: Merck built an internal generative AI platform to accelerate authoring of clinical study reports (CSRs) within its clinical development process. The implementation combines advanced table pre-processing with large language models (LLMs) and a proprietary gen-AI authoring platform. Clinical study data and tables are mapped, extracted, styled, and validated before the LLM-driven authoring step generates a high-quality first draft for qualified medical writers to review. Merck also changed its operating model around the platform, training teams in prompt engineering and data pipelines so they could supervise outputs and manage the workflow safely. The system is designed for rigorous human oversight rather than autonomous submission, and it has already been used across multiple studies and in live CSR submissions. Merck is now scaling the platform across its late-phase pipeline.

data_flow: Clinical study data and tables are ingested into Merck's proprietary platform, where advanced table pre-processing handles mapping, extraction, styling, and validation. That prepared content is passed to LLM-based gen AI authoring to generate a CSR first draft, which is then reviewed by qualified medical writers before use in Merck's clinical study reporting workflow.
business_outcome: Merck shortened the creation of fully human-reviewed first drafts of clinical study reports, improved draft quality, and accelerated the path to making medicines available to health care providers and patients.
